agents.name: Claude Code
agents.quote: Personally, I write a lot of my code from the iOS app. It's a convenient way to make changes without opening a laptop.

history.quote: I run 5 Claudes in parallel in my terminal. I number my tabs 1-5, and use system notifications to know when a Claude needs input

agents.name: Claude Tag
agents.quote: The setup is straightforward: we have a Slack channel called proj-claude-maintains-apps. In it, Claude Tag runs a bunch of daily routines across iOS, Android, Desktop, web, CLI, and Agent SDK:

models.name: Fable 5.1
models.quote: This model is a pleasure to work with, and I've been using it for everything.

history.quote: I use Opus 4.5 with thinking for everything.
Personally, I use xhigh effort for most tasks, and max effort for the hardest tasks.
Fable is the best model I have used for coding, by a wide margin.

review_style.value: Reads diffs only for critical code
review_style.quote: I read diffs when it's touching critical code, or code that's important to get right. I don't write the code.

also.quote: Personally, I’ve been using it for a few weeks and have found it catches many real bugs that I would not have noticed otherwise
The model has reached a point where I generally  trust it to run the right commands and make the right edits. I just look at the final result.

harness.value: Git worktrees, dozens of parallel Claudes
harness.quote: Worktrees are essential for doing lots of parallel work in the same repository. I have dozens of Claudes running at all times, and this is how I do it.

history.quote: Most sessions start in Plan mode (shift+tab twice).
Personally, I use multiple git checkouts, but most of the Claude Code team prefers worktrees

parallelism.quote: I run 5 Claudes in parallel in my terminal.

rules_files.value: Team CLAUDE.md in git, updated on every Claude mistake
rules_files.quote: Anytime we see Claude do something incorrectly we add it to the http://CLAUDE.md, so Claude knows not to do it next time.

mcp_servers.quote: The Slack MCP configuration is checked into our .mcp.json and shared with the team.

value: Stop hook to verify long runs
hooks.quote: We use a PostToolUse hook to format Claude's code.

signature.caption: test, /simplify, open PR
signature.why: Our pick: one skill at the end of most prompts puts his verify-first rule into practice. Claude tests its own work end to end before it opens a PR.
signature.quote:
Personally, many of my prompts these days look like "Claude do blah blah /go". /go is a skill that has Claude

1. Test itself end to end using bash, browser, or computer use
2. Run the /simplify skill
3. Put up a PR

archetype.why: Dozens of Claudes in worktrees, plus loops and routines that ship PRs without him.

signature_quote.value: give Claude a way to verify its work.
signature_quote.more: If Claude has that feedback loop, it will 2-3x the quality of the final result.
